source.publication: 2025 IT-40 Full-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Booklet
source.section: Schedule 3 line 1 (PDF page 24: joint 2,000, all other filers 1,000), line 4 (PDF page 25: 1,000 age 65 or older), line 5 (PDF page 25: 500 age 65 or older and IT-40 line 1 under 40,000, or under 20,000 married filing separately); Schedule 1 line 3 and PDF page 13 Line 3 (OOS municipal obligation interest add-back; Indiana's own obligations are not added back); Form IT-40 lines 1-8 (PDF page 1; line 8 'multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)'); booklet PDF page 8 Line 1; PDF pages 5-6 rounding

worked: Federal AGI = private pension person 0 38,000.00 = 38,000.00. Federal taxable income = 38,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 20,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Indiana starts from federal AGI). Form IT-40 line 1 federal AGI 38,000.00. Schedule 1 line 3 OOS municipal interest add-back 5,000.00; Indiana's own obligations 3,000.00 are not added back; neither is in federal AGI. Line 2 add-backs 5,000.00; line 3 = 38,000.00 + 5,000.00 = 43,000.00. Schedule 2: no deductions; line 12 total = 0.00. IT-40 line 4 = 0.00. Line 5 = 43,000.00 - 0.00 = 43,000.00. Schedule 3: line 1 1,000.00; line 4 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00; line 5 IT-40 line 1 38,000.00 is under 40,000.00: 1 x 500.00 = 500.00; line 7 total = 2,500.00. IT-40 line 6 = 2,500.00. Line 7 = 43,000.00 - 2,500.00 = 40,500.00. Line 8 = 40,500.00 x 0.03 = 1,215.00. No credits; county tax (line 9) is local and out of scope. State income tax 1,215.00. The 500 test reads IT-40 line 1 (38,000.00), not line 3 (43,000.00), so the add-back does not cost the 500. The other-state interest is taken as from an obligation acquired after Dec. 31, 2011; on that footing the booklet gives the same result. The projection's muni_interest.treatment other_states_taxed_own_exempt is followed: own-state interest is not added.
accepted_approximations: All municipal bond interest is treated as from other states and taxed; Indiana's own obligations are not added back, nor are other states' obligations held or acquired before Jan. 1, 2012.
